key_insight: Charge disproportionation in SmNiO3 can reorganize to screen polar discontinuities at ferroelectric interfaces, turning Ni sites into more uniform valence states at each interface depending on BaTiO3 polarization direction.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a tunable mechanism for stabilizing oxide superlattices and controlling interfacial charge in perovskite device stacks by choosing polarization orientation and interface termination.
method: Compare two interface terminations: NiO2–BaO and SmO–TiO2
Analyze how BaTiO3 polarization changes polar discontinuity and Ni charge disproportionation
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a specific screening response: transfer of 1 e/f.u. between interfaces and a disproportionation change from Ni4+/Ni2+ to Ni2+/Ni2+ and Ni4+/Ni4+ at opposite interfaces.
watch_item: The screening mechanism may not be sufficient for larger polar discontinuities, which may require more complex disproportionation patterns and could limit straightforward device implementation.
paper_title: Polar discontinuity screening by charge disproportionation in ferroelectric-nickelate superlattices
